verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要审问审问这流人血的城吗？当使她知道她一切可憎的事。
verses.en: “As for you, son of man, are you willing to pronounce judgment?[NOTE:1] Are you willing to pronounce judgment on the bloody city?[NOTE:2] Then confront her with all her abominable deeds!
notes: Heb “will you judge.” Here the imperfect form of the verb is probably used with a desiderative nuance. Addressed to the prophet, “judge” means to warn of or pronounce God’s impending judgment upon the city. See 20:4.
The phrase “bloody city” is used of Nineveh in Nah 3:1.

verses.zh: 你要说，主耶和华如此说：哎！这城有流人血的事在其中，叫她受报的日期来到，又做偶像玷污自己，陷害自己。
verses.en: Then say, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: O city, who spills blood within herself (which brings on her doom),[NOTE:1] and who makes herself idols (which results in impurity),
notes: Heb “her time”; this refers to the time of impending judgment (see the note on “doom” in v. 4).

verses.zh: 你因流了人的血，就为有罪；你做了偶像，就玷污自己，使你受报之日临近，报应之年来到。所以我叫你受列国的凌辱和列邦的讥诮。
verses.en: you are guilty because of the blood you shed and defiled by the idols you made. You have hastened the day of your doom;[NOTE:1] the end of your years has come.[NOTE:2] Therefore I will make[NOTE:3] you an object of scorn to the nations, an object to be mocked by all lands.
notes: Heb “you have brought near your days.” The expression “bring near your days” appears to be an adaptation of the idiom “days draw near,” which is used to indicate that an event, such as death, is imminent (see Gen 27:41; 47:29; Deut 31:14; 1 Kgs 2:1; Ezek 12:23). Here “your days” probably refer to the days of the personified city’s life, which was about to come to an end through God’s judgment.

Heb “and you have come to your years.” This appears to mean that she has arrived at the time when her years (i.e., life) would end, though it may mean that her years of punishment will begin. Because “day” and “time” are so closely associated in the immediate context (see 21:25, 29), some prefer to emend the text and read: “you have brought near your time.” See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:31, as well as the translator’s note on verse 3.
The Hebrew verb is a prophetic perfect, emphasizing that the action is as good as done from the speaker’s perspective.

verses.zh: 你这名臭、多乱的城啊，那些离你近、离你远的都必讥诮你。
verses.en: Those both near and far from you will mock you, you with your bad reputation,[NOTE:1] full of turmoil.
notes: Heb “unclean of name.”

verses.zh: 「看哪，以色列的首领各逞其能，在你中间流人之血。
verses.en: “‘See how each of the princes of Israel living within you has used his authority to shed blood.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Look! The princes of Israel, each according to his arm, were in you in order to shed blood.”

verses.zh: 在你中间有轻慢父母的，有欺压寄居的，有亏负孤儿寡妇的。
verses.en: They have treated father and mother with contempt[NOTE:1] within you; they have oppressed the resident foreigner among you; they have wronged the orphan and the widow[NOTE:2] within you.
notes: Heb “treated lightly, cursed.”
Widows and orphans are often coupled together in the OT (Deut 14:29; 16:11, 14; 24:19-21; 26:12-13; Jer 7:6; 22:3). They represented all who were poor and vulnerable to economic exploitation.

verses.zh: 你藐视了我的圣物，干犯了我的安息日。
verses.en: You have despised my holy things and desecrated my Sabbaths!

verses.zh: 在你中间有谗谤人、流人血的；有在山上吃过祭偶像之物的，有行淫乱的。
verses.en: Slanderous men shed blood within you.[NOTE:1] Those who live within you eat pagan sacrifices on the mountains;[NOTE:2] they commit obscene acts among you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “men of slander are in you in order to shed blood.”
Heb “and on the mountains they eat within you.” The mountains mentioned here were the site of pagan sacrifices. See 18:6.
This statement introduces vv. 10-11 and refers in general terms to the sexual sins described there. For the legal background of vv. 10-11, see Lev 18:7-20; 20:10-21; Deut 22:22-23, 30; 27:22.

verses.zh: 在你中间有露继母下体羞辱父亲的，有玷辱月经不洁净之妇人的。
verses.en: They have sexual relations with their father’s wife within you;[NOTE:1] they violate women during their menstrual period within you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “The nakedness of a father one uncovers within you.” The ancient versions read the verb as plural (“they uncover”). If the singular is retained, it must be taken as indefinite and representative of the entire group. The idiomatic expression “uncover the nakedness” refers here to sexual intercourse (cf. Lev 18:6). To uncover a father’s nakedness could include sexual relations with one’s own mother (Lev 18:7), but more likely it refers to having intercourse with another wife of one’s father, such as a stepmother (Lev 18:8; cf. Gen 35:22; 49:4).

Heb “(one who is) unclean due to the impurity they humble within you.” The use of the verb “to humble” suggests that these men forced themselves upon women during menstruation. Having sexual relations with a woman during her period was forbidden by the Law (Lev 18:19; 20:18).

verses.zh: 这人与邻舍的妻行可憎的事；那人贪淫玷污儿妇；还有玷辱同父之姊妹的。
verses.en: One[NOTE:1] commits an abominable act with his neighbor’s wife; another obscenely defiles his daughter-in-law; another violates[NOTE:2] his sister—his father’s daughter[NOTE:3]—within you.
notes: Heb “a man.”
The verb is the same one used in verse 10b and suggests forcible sexual violation of the woman.
Sexual relations with one’s half-sister may be primarily in view here. See Lev 18:9 and 20:17.

verses.zh: 在你中间有为流人血受贿赂的；有向借钱的弟兄取利，向借粮的弟兄多要的。且因贪得无餍，欺压邻舍夺取财物，竟忘了我。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: They take bribes within you to shed blood. You engage in usury and charge interest;[NOTE:1] you extort money from your neighbors. You have forgotten me,[NOTE:2] declares the Sovereign Lord.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “usury and interest you take.” See 18:13, 17. This kind of economic exploitation violated the law given in Lev 25:36.
Forgetting the Lord is also addressed in Deut 6:12; 8:11, 14; Jer 3:21; 13:25; Ezek 23:35; Hos 2:15; 8:14; 13:6.
The second person verb forms are feminine singular in Hebrew, indicating that the personified city is addressed here as representing its citizens.

verses.zh: 「看哪，我因你所得不义之财和你中间所流的血，就拍掌叹息。
verses.en: “‘See, I strike my hands together[NOTE:1] at the dishonest profit you have made and at the bloodshed[NOTE:2] they have done among you.
notes: This gesture apparently expresses mourning and/or anger (see 6:11; 21:14, 17).
Heb “the blood that was in you.”

verses.zh: 到了我惩罚你的日子，你的心还能忍受吗？你的手还能有力吗？我―耶和华说了这话，就必照着行。
verses.en: Can your heart endure[NOTE:1] or can your hands be strong when I deal with you?[NOTE:2] I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will do it!
notes: Heb “stand.” The heart here stands for the emotions; Jerusalem would panic in the face of God’s judgment.
Heb “in the days when I act against you.”

verses.zh: 我必将你分散在列国，四散在列邦。我也必从你中间除掉你的污秽。
verses.en: I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you among various countries; I will remove your impurity from you.[NOTE:1]
notes: The ultimate purpose of divine judgment is to purify the covenant community of its sins.

verses.zh: 你必在列国人的眼前因自己所行的被亵渎，你就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: You will be profaned within yourself[NOTE:1] in the sight of the nations; then you will know that I am the Lord.’”
notes: The phrase “within yourself” is the same as the several previous occurrences of “within you” but adjusted to fit this clause, which is the culmination of the series of indictments. tc Several ancient versions read the verb as first person, in which case the Lord refers to how his people’s sin brings disgrace upon him. For a defense of the Hebrew text, see D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:712, n. 68, and M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:457-58.

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，以色列家在我看为渣滓。他们都是炉中的铜、锡、铁、铅，都是银渣滓。
verses.en: “Son of man, the house of Israel has become slag to me. All of them are like bronze, tin, iron, and lead in the furnace;[NOTE:1] they are the worthless slag of silver.
notes: For similar imagery, see Isa 1:21-26 and Jer 6:27-30.

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：因你们都成为渣滓，我必聚集你们在耶路撒冷中。
verses.en: Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: ‘Because all of you[NOTE:1] have become slag, look out! I am about to gather you in the middle of Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew second person pronoun is masculine plural here and in vv. 19b-21, indicating that the people are being addressed.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 人怎样将银、铜、铁、铅、锡聚在炉中，吹火熔化；照样，我也要发怒气和忿怒，将你们聚集放在城中，熔化你们。
verses.en: As silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin are gathered in a furnace so that the fire can blow on them to melt them, so I will gather you in my anger and in my rage. I will deposit you there[NOTE:1] and melt you.
notes: Heb “I will put.” No object is supplied in the Hebrew, prompting many to emend the text to “I will blow.” See BHS and verse 21.

verses.zh: 我必聚集你们，把我烈怒的火吹在你们身上，你们就在其中熔化。
verses.en: I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of my fury, and you will be melted in it.

verses.zh: 银子怎样熔化在炉中，你们也必照样熔化在城中，你们就知道我―耶和华是将忿怒倒在你们身上了。」
verses.en: As silver is melted in a furnace, so you will be melted in it, and you will know that I, the Lord, have poured out my anger on you.’”

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要对这地说：你是未得洁净之地，在恼恨的日子也没有雨下在你以上。
verses.en: “Son of man, say to her: ‘You are a land that receives no rain[NOTE:1] or showers in the day of my anger.’[NOTE:2]
notes: The MT reads: “that is not cleansed”; the LXX reads: “that is not drenched,” which assumes a different vowel pointing as well as the loss of a מ (mem) due to haplography. In light of the following reference to showers, the reading of the LXX certainly fits the context well. For a defense of the emendation, see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:32. Yet the MT is not an unreasonable reading since uncleanness in the land also fits the context. A poetic connection between rain and the land being uncleansed may be feasible since washing with water is elsewhere associated with cleansing (Num 8:7; 31:23; Ps 51:7).
Heb “in a day of anger.”

verses.zh: 其中的先知同谋背叛，如咆哮的狮子抓撕掠物。他们吞灭人民，抢夺财宝，使这地多有寡妇。
verses.en: Her princes[NOTE:1] within her are like a roaring lion tearing its prey; they have devoured lives. They take away riches and valuable things; they have made many women widows[NOTE:2] within it.
notes: Heb “a conspiracy of her prophets is in her midst.” The LXX reads “whose princes” rather than “a conspiracy of prophets.” The prophets are mentioned later in the paragraph (v. 28). If one follows the LXX in verse 25, then five distinct groups are mentioned in vv. 25-29: princes, priests, officials, prophets, and the people of the land. For a defense of the Septuagintal reading, see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:32, and D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:720, n. 4.
Heb “her widows they have multiplied.” The statement alludes to their murderous acts.

verses.zh: 其中的祭司强解我的律法，亵渎我的圣物，不分别圣的和俗的，也不使人分辨洁净的和不洁净的，又遮眼不顾我的安息日；我也在他们中间被亵慢。
verses.en: Her priests abuse my law and have desecrated my holy things. They do not distinguish between the holy and the profane[NOTE:1] or recognize any distinction between the unclean and the clean. They ignore[NOTE:2] my Sabbaths, and I am profaned in their midst.
notes: Or “between the consecrated and the common.”
Heb “hide their eyes from.” The idiom means to disregard or ignore something or someone (see Lev 20:4; 1 Sam 12:3; Prov 28:27; Isa 1:15).

verses.zh: 其中的首领彷佛豺狼抓撕掠物，杀人流血，伤害人命，要得不义之财。
verses.en: Her officials are like wolves in her midst rending their prey—shedding blood and destroying lives—so they can get dishonest profit.

verses.zh: 其中的先知为百姓用未泡透的灰抹墙，就是为他们见虚假的异象，用谎诈的占卜，说：『主耶和华如此说』，其实耶和华没有说。
verses.en: Her prophets coat their messages with whitewash.[NOTE:1] They see false visions and announce lying omens for them, saying, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says,’ when the Lord has not spoken.
notes: Heb “Her prophets coat for themselves with whitewash.” The expression may be based on Ezek 13:10-15.

verses.zh: 国内众民一味地欺压，惯行抢夺，亏负困苦穷乏的，背理欺压寄居的。
verses.en: The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery. They have wronged the poor and needy; they have oppressed the resident foreigner and denied them justice.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the resident foreigner they have oppressed without justice.”

verses.zh: 我在他们中间寻找一人重修墙垣，在我面前为这国站在破口防堵，使我不灭绝这国，却找不着一个。
verses.en: “I looked for a man from among them who would repair the wall and stand in the gap before me on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it, but I found no one.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “I did not find.”

verses.zh: 所以我将恼恨倒在他们身上，用烈怒的火灭了他们，照他们所行的报应在他们头上。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: So I have poured my anger on them and destroyed them with the fire of my fury. I hereby repay them for what they have done,[NOTE:1] declares the Sovereign Lord.”
notes: Heb “their way on their head I have placed.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the four modern translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Third paragraph, etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 22:1-5

1Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying, 2"And you,
son of man, will you judge, will you judge the bloody city? Then cause her to know all her abominations. 3You shall say, 'Thus says the Lord
God, "A city shedding blood in her midst, so that her time will come, and that makes idols, contrary to her interest, for defilement!
4You have become guilty by the blood which you have shed, and defiled by your idols which you have made. Thus you have brought your day near and have
come to your years; therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mocking to all the lands. 5Those who are near and those who are far from you
will mock you, you of ill repute, full of turmoil."'"

22:2 "Then the word of the Lord came to me saying" See note at Ezek. 21:1.

▣ "son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

▣ "will you judge, will you judge" The repetition of the VERB (BDB 1047, KB 1622, Qal IMPERFECT
SINGULAR) is for emphasis (cf. Ezek. 20:4). Ezekiel acted as both prosecutor and judge on YHWH's behalf (cf. Ezek. 23:36). He lays out the
charges and the consequences, then because of no intercessor or repentance (cf. Ezek. 22:30-31) they are implemented (i.e. 586 B.C.)!

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta
"the bloody city"

TEV
"the city that is full of

murderers"

NJB
"blood-stained city"

JPSOA, Rotherham
"the city of bloodshed"

LXX
"the city of streams of blood"

REB
"the murderous city"

Jerusalem was bloody in two senses.

- murder, injustice (vv. 3b, 4a, 9a, cf. 2 Kgs. 21:6)

- idolatrous sacrifices (vv. 3c, 4b, 9b)

This is the key CONSTRUCT (BDB 746, 196) used throughout this chapter (cf. Ezek. 22:2 [twice],
3,4,6,9,12,13). It is used of Nineveh in Nahum 3:1. Some think it is used of Jerusalem because of

- the worship of Molech (cf. Ezek. 16:21; 20:26,31; 23:37)

- the killing of the righteous (cf. Ezek. 22:25)

It is historically possible that Nebuchadnezzar's initial raid in 588 B.C. caused the population of the area
to seek refuge in the walled city of Jerusalem, but instead of refuge they found exploitation and death by their own countrymen!

In 586 B.C. the city and temple were destroyed by Neo-Babylon's army and the populace who escaped
the sword were exiled to Babylon.

▣ "cause her to know" See SPECIAL TOPIC: Know (using mostly Deuteronomy as a paradigm)

▣ "abomination" See Special Topic: Abomination.

22:3 "for defilement" This VERB (BDB 379, KB 375, Qal INFINITIVE) means to become
unclean because of her creation of and association with foreign pagan idols (cf. Ezek. 22:4).

This defilement (Qal PERFECT in Ezek. 22:4, i.e. uncleanness) is also described in Ezek. 22:4.
Ezekiel, being a priest, was well trained in the laws of Leviticus.

- I have made you a reproach (BDB 357) to the nations, cf. Ezek. 5:14,15; 16:57

- I have made you a mocking (BDB 887) to all lands, cf. VERB (Hithpael IMPERFECT) in
Ezek. 22:5 (Hithpael only 3 times in the OT, 2 Kgs. 2:23; Hab. 1:10; and Piel only once, Ezek. 16:31).

- you of ill repute (BDB 1027, lit. "infamous one," Ezek. 22:5

There is a parallelism among

- the nations, Ezek. 22:4

- all the lands, Ezek. 22:4

- those who are near. . .far, Ezek. 22:5

All people will be affected by Judah's sin (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6)! Judah's actions affect the way the world
understands YHWH. The same is true as to the way the church's sin and false teachers confuse the world about Jesus!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

22:4 "thus you have brought your day near" YHWH asserts that their sin has hastened the day of their
judgment (e.g. 2 Pet. 3:12)!

22:5 "you of ill repute, full of turmoil" These are two characterizations of Judah.

- "of ill repute" is literally a Hebrew CONSTRUCT (BDB 379, 1027)
"polluted name." They are considered ceremonially unclean and thereby cannot approach YHWH.

- "full of turmoil" is literally a Hebrew CONSTRUCT (BDB 912, 223), "full of confusion," which is a "Holy War"
term (cf. Exod. 14:24; 23:27; Deut. 7:23). The tragedy is that now YHWH fights against His polluted people (cf. Deut. 28:20)! Isaiah 22:5
describes an eschatological scene (cf. Ezek. 7:5-9, esp. Ezek. 22:7).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 22:6-12

6"Behold, the rulers of Israel, each according to his power, have been in you for the purpose
of shedding blood. 7They have treated father and mother lightly within you. The alien they have oppressed in your midst; the fatherless and the
widow they have wronged in you. 8You have despised My holy things and profaned My sabbaths. 9Slanderous men have been in you
for the purpose of shedding blood, and in you they have eaten at the mountain shrines. In your midst they have committed acts of lewdness. 10In
you they have uncovered their fathers' nakedness; in you they have humbled her who was unclean in her menstrual impurity. 11One has committed
abomination with his neighbor's wife and another has lewdly defiled his daughter-in-law. And another in you has humbled his sister, his father's daughter. 12In
you they have taken bribes to shed blood; you have taken interest and profits, and you have injured your neighbors for gain by oppression, and you have forgotten Me,"
declares the Lord God.

22:6-12 First, Ezekiel lists (PERFECT TENSE) the settled rebellious attitude of Judah's political leaders, especially
the kings in violation of the Mosaic Covenant.

- shed blood, Ezek. 22:6

- treated fathers and mothers lightly, Ezek. 22:7

- oppressed the alien, fatherless, and widows, Ezek. 22:7 (cf. Jer. 7:6; 22:3)

Then he lists the sins of Judah (cf. Jer. 7:5-11; Isa. 1).

- despised YHWH's holy things, Ezek. 22:8

- profaned YHWH's sabbaths, cf. Ezek. 20:13,16,21,24; 23:38

- lied (i.e. slandered, cf. Lev. 19:16), Ezek. 22:9

- worshiped idols (i.e. shed blood and eaten at mountain shrines, fertility worship, cf. Ezek. 18:6,11),
Ezek. 22:9

- committed acts of lewdness, Ezek. 22:9

- uncovered their father's nakedness (sexual contact with mother or another of his father's wives,
cf. Leviticus 18), Ezek. 22:10

- sex with women during menstrual period (cf. Lev. 18:19), Ezek. 22:10

- sex with neighbor's wife (cf. Lev. 18:20; 20:10), Ezek. 22:11

- lewdly defiled his daughter-in-law (cf. Lev. 20:12), Ezek. 22:11

- humbled his sister (or half sister), his father's daughter, in a sexual sense (cf. Lev. 20:17), Ezek. 22:11

- took money to commit murder (cf. Deut. 27:25), Ezek. 22:12

- loaned money with interest (cf. Ezek. 18:13; Lev. 25:36,37; Deut. 23:19,20; Prov. 28:8), Ezek. 22:12

- took advantage of neighbors, Ezek. 22:12

- forgot YHWH (cf. Ezek. 23:35; Deut. 6:12; 8:11,14; Isa. 17:10; Jer. 3:21; 13:25; Hosea 2:15; 8:14; 13:6), Ezek. 22:12 (also 23:35)

The Mosaic Covenant and common decency had been lost to Canaanite fertility worship. Ezekiel
tries to embarrass Judah by using shocking language related to their fertility worship (cf. Ezek. 16:27; 43; 58;
22:9,11; 23:21,27,29,35,44,48,49; 24:13)!

22:7 "treated their father and mother lightly" See Exod. 20:12; 21:17; Lev. 20:9; and Deut. 27:16.

Special Topic: Honor Father and Mother

▣ "the widow" See Exod. 22:22-24 and Deut. 24:17; 27:19.

22:9 "slanderous men" See Lev. 19:16.

22:10 "uncover their fathers' nakedness" This seems to refer to sexual intercourse with a father's former wife,
stepmother, or concubine (cf. Lev. 18:7, 8; 20:11; Deut. 22:30; 27:20).

Special Topic: Abomination

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 22:13-16

13"Behold, then, I smite My hand at your dishonest gain which you have acquired and at the
bloodshed which is among you. 14Can your heart endure, or can your hands be strong in the days that I will deal with you? I, the Lord,
have spoken and will act. 15I will scatter you among the nations and I will disperse you through the lands, and I will consume your uncleanness from you.
16You will profane yourself in the sight of the nations, and you will know that I am the Lord."

22:13 "I strike my hand" See note at Ezek. 21:14.

Special Topic: Hand

22:14 This is an allusion to Ezek. 21:7.

▣ "I, the Lord, have spoken and will act" This is a recurrent theme of
Ezekiel which emphasizes

- YHWH's control of world events

- the fact that YHWH's word can be trusted and depended on (i.e. Isa. 55:9-11)

- the fact that judgment is coming, repentance (i.e. conditional covenant) is no longer possible

22:15 The threat of removal from the Promised Land for covenant disobedience goes back to Lev. 26:33
and Deut. 4:27; 28:64; 29:28. YHWH removed the Canaanites from Canaan because of their sins (cf. Gen. 15:12-21),
now He will remove Judah. He is no respecter of persons, shows no favoritism!

The VERBS "scatter" (BDB 806, KB 918, Hiphil PERFECT with
waw; cf. Ezek. 12:15; 20:23,24) and "disperse" (BDB 279, KB 280,Piel PERFECT with waw;
cf. Ezek. 5:10,12; 6:8; 12:15; 20:23; 36:19) are most often used of Israel's and Judah's exiles, but they are also used of YHWH's
judgment on Egypt, 29:12,13; 30:23,26. Egypt was the source of idolatry (cf. Ezek. 23:27,48). YHWH must cleanse His people of this pollution.

The same VERBS are used to describe YHWH's fighting on Israel's behalf (i.e. Num. 10:35), but now
He fights against them because they have become abominations like the ten Canaanite tribes. They must be removed from YHWH's land, which they are polluting!

Special Topic: Pre-Israelite Inhabitants of Palestine)

YHWH's purpose in the Assyrian and Babylonian exiles was the purification of His people! YHWH wants a righteous people who
reflect His character to a lost world so that they may know Him and come to Him!

The MT has "you," but several ancient versions (LXX, Peshitta, Vulgate) change this to "I."
The second part of the verse lends support for the MT, but Ezek. 22:26 tends to support the versions. The UBS
Hebrew OT Project, p. 71, gives "I" a "C" rating (considerable doubt). If "I" is correct, YHWH's people's sinning brought shame to Him!

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 22:17-22

17And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, 18"Son
of man, the house of Israel has become dross to Me; all of them are bronze and tin and iron and lead in the furnace; they are the dross of silver. 19Therefore,
thus says the Lord God, 'Because all of you have become dross, therefore, behold, I am going to gather you into the midst of Jerusalem.
20As they gather silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin into the furnace to blow fire on it in order to melt it, so I will gather you in My anger
and in My wrath and I will lay you there and melt you. 21I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of My wrath, and you will be melted in the midst of it.
22As silver is melted in the furnace, so you will be melted in the midst of it; and you will know that I, the Lord, have poured out My wrath on you.'"

22:17-22 This is imagery from ancient metallurgy. YHWH calls Jerusalem a mixture of metals, which made
them absolutely useless (cf. Jer. 6:27-30). The mixture was the Mosaic Covenant with Egyptian idolatry and
Canaanite idolatry. YHWH would melt them so as to remove the useless metals (cf. Isa. 1:22,25).

22:21 As so often Ezekiel uses terms normally reserved for a positive connotation in a shockingly negative
way. In this verse "gather" (BDB 488, KB 484, Piel PERFECT with waw)
is used in a judgment sense, but usually it refers to a gathering of Israelites from among the nations where
they have been exiled (cf. Ezek. 39:28; Ps. 147:2).

22:24 "is not cleansed or rained on" This is a very difficult verse. Some think it refers to (1) no human tending and no divine rain
or (2) no cleansing rain. For sure God's judgment has fallen and no moisture came (sign of judgment in Deuteronomy).

22:29 "The people of the land" This term originally (and here) meant "landed owners with full rights as
citizens" (cf. Ezek. 12:19; 45:16,22; 46:3), but after the Exile it referred to the poorest people of the land
(cf. the use in the NT).

Special Topic: The People of the Land

22:30 This is such a shocking verse, which mirrors Isa. 59:16; 63:5 and Jer. 5:1. There was no one!
What was YHWH looking for? Someone to

- build up the wall, cf. Ezek. 13:5; Ps. 106:23

- stand in the gap (intercede in prayer on behalf of Judah as Moses and Samuel had, cf. Jer. 15:1, which is similar to Ezek. 14:14,20; 33:1-6)

It is surprising that Ezekiel himself did not fulfill this text, but remember the setting is Jerusalem,
not the exiles in Babylon. But then Jeremiah was in Jerusalem, why did he not fulfill this search? The verse is a
literary hyperbole. It is not meant to be taken literally. It is for shock value only! There were some righteous
people in Jerusalem (cf. Ezek. 20:47; 21:4).

The good news is that YHWH seeks intercessors! He wants to be convinced to withhold judgment.
He wants to forgive, but no one interceded and people did not repent!
